item_taken.first_six_words: Mercy without a scene: a concession
item_taken.why: The alternative acts through the conceding party: Ostrava's 9 October level, its draft offer, its offer-file note 'granted against the Kestrel return', and the 20 November contract are all carriers on Ostrava's side of a return that never happened and had stopped existing five weeks before signature, while the neighbours do not fit: Winner's negative needs a surviving prohibition, Permission ash needs people declining because they expect a prohibition, and Missing alarm needs a response triggered by the nonarrival, whereas here the concession came on 9 October before the 15 October date and Kestrel's plan was drawn up without reference to her, so nothing responded to her nonarrival at all.

reasoning: The rule's first clause applies directly. The return was absorbed at the counterparty's next planning cycle: Kestrel's headcount plan locks every 15 October, was drawn up without reference to her, and on 15 October 2026 folded her line into two existing posts. Nobody opposed it: no one at Kestrel had organized a use for her desk, the two engineers taking her duties had not asked for them, no one was asked about her, and no one opposed or declined her return. The second clause does not fire: a reserved place that acquires beneficiaries who then oppose the return would need someone at Kestrel with a stake in her desk who resisted her coming back, and the case records the absence of exactly that. So the return goes to option-expiries under 'a counterparty's transfer or planning cycle', a clock the holder never started. The rule sorts only on the Kestrel-side facts; the Ostrava-side carriers (the conceded level, the note, the late contract) are not what the rule decides on, and they cross as concrete facts about how the option was used before it expired, not as a second claim.
case_out: A previously available course of action, Ines Farro's return to Kestrel Systems under an undated letter promising an equivalent post after open-ended unpaid leave since 1 September 2025, became unexercisable on 15 October 2026 without her declining it (she sent Kestrel nothing between 20 August and 15 October 2026 and never returned) and without any party at her own table deciding about it: Kestrel's headcount plan was drawn up without reference to her, no one at Kestrel was asked about her, and no one opposed or declined her return. Condition lost: a counterparty, Kestrel's line for her, which the plan folded into two existing posts on 15 October 2026; employment there afterwards was a new hire from outside. Carrier that runs the clock: Kestrel's headcount plan, which locks every 15 October. Last intervention that could have kept it: the case does not name one; it records only that she sent Kestrel nothing between 20 August and the 15 October lock. Sort: a counterparty's transfer or planning cycle, a clock the holder never started. Before it expired the option was represented once, in her letter of 20 August 2026 to Ostrava Labs ('Kestrel's plan locks on 15 October and my post lapses with it; settle the level before then or I go back'), and was priced by Ostrava within the negotiation of its offer (August to November 2026): Ostrava conceded the level on 9 October 2026, wrote it into the draft offer, and noted in the offer file that the level was 'granted against the Kestrel return'. The contract she signed on 20 November 2026 at that level was issued only after an export-control screening completed on 18 November, five weeks after the return had stopped being exercisable.
